title: Complete Magnetic Hierarchy in Bichromatically Driven Unconventional Magnets
authors: Pei-Hao Fu, Sayed Ali Akbar Ghorash
abstract: We establish a general framework for engineering unconventional magnetism using bichromatic driving. We identify a sharp hierarchy: for a bichromatic drive with a generic even commensurate frequency ratio, the leading continuum $q$-wave magnet generates components only up to order $q-2$, whereas lattice higher-gradient terms supply the missing $q-1$ and $q$ parities and complete the hierarchy through order $q$. We explicitly illustrate this new revised hierarchy on a $d$-wave altermagnet irradiated by a circularly-linearly polarized light, and show that the asymmetry of the driving field is transferred to the light-dressed electronic structure, producing momentum-asymmetric dispersions beyond the static and single-frequency limits. We further show that this band asymmetry is absent in the leading continuum expansion and originates from higher-gradient lattice terms that are converted by the bichromatic drive into odd-in-momentum contributions. Extending the analysis to higher-order unconventional magnets, we further obtain complete magnetic hierarchies for all $q$-parity unconventional magnets. Our results establish bichromatic Floquet driving as a general route for generating mixed-parity magnetic hierarchies and dynamically engineering unconventional magnetism.
summary: This work develops a general theory showing how bichromatic light driving can systematically engineer unconventional magnetism in materials. By analyzing the effective Hamiltonian, the authors demonstrate that the drive completes the magnetic spin-splitting hierarchy up to a specific order $q$. This mechanism is powerful because it allows for the dynamic generation of mixed-parity magnetic components, which is crucial for advanced spintronic applications.
main_problem: The paper establishes a general framework for engineering unconventional magnetism by using bichromatic light driving to induce a complete magnetic hierarchy of spin-splitting components.
main_result: The bichromatic drive can complete the magnetic hierarchy up to order $q$ by combining the leading continuum theory results with contributions from higher-gradient lattice terms, enabling magnetic-parity conversion.
method: The analysis employs Floquet engineering theory to derive the effective time-averaged Hamiltonian, comparing continuum approximations with full lattice treatments.
model_or_system: The system models unconventional magnets (altermagnets) characterized by specific magnetic parities, driven by a bichromatic field composed of circularly and linearly polarized light.
key_observables: Magnetic spin-splitting components classified by angular harmonics ($s, p, d, f, g, \dots$), and the resulting momentum-asymmetric electronic structure.
important_parameters: The frequency ratio of the bichromatic drive (especially generic even commensurate ratios) and the lattice structure details.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the assumption of a generic even commensurate frequency ratio for hierarchy completion, and approximations are made when comparing continuum vs. lattice results.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the schematic of $d$-wave magnets under driving, showing band dispersions and confirming the completion of the $s$-$p$-$d$ hierarchy.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first establishing the general framework for hierarchy completion using $d$-wave magnets, then detailing the mechanism of parity conversion, and finally extending the analysis to higher-order magnets ($f$-wave, $g$-wave) to show the general $s-p-d-f-g$ hierarchy.
why_interesting: The use of Floquet engineering to dynamically control and engineer specific symmetries (like parity) in magnetic order parameters is highly relevant to open quantum systems and quantum optics applications.

Spintronics.note: The new paper directly addresses engineering unconventional magnetism in materials using light driving, which strongly overlaps with the theme of quantum-optics concepts applied to magnetic systems, particularly in the context of spin-splitting.
